parole.testo: Borrowed from German Zwickel, more specifically from Bavarian zwickel.
Borrowed from German Zeche; more specifically, from Bavarian Zech in one of its obsolete senses "association" or "get-together", from Middle High German zech, zeche.
From German Nockerl (“dumpling”), from Bavarian [Term?], + -dli. Suffixed with -i to resolve the word-final consonant cluster, compare cetli from Bavarian zettl or German Zettel (/⁠ˈt͡sɛtl̩⁠/) etc.

parole.significato: any of various old units of volume, often equivalent to about 1.4–1.6 litres
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Pinte and Bavarian Pint, from French pinte, from Vulgar Latin *pincta (“mark used to indicate level on vessels”), from Latin pictus (“painted”), from Latin pingō (“to paint”). Compare English pint.

parole.significato: cooper (a craftsman who makes and repairs barrels and similar wooden vessels such as casks, buckets and tubs)
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Binder, more specifically from Bavarian binder.
First attested in 1542. From German Schanze (more specifically from Bavarian [Term?]).

parole.significato: gravel (small round pebbles used in construction)
parole.testo: Borrowed from German, more specifically from Bavarian. Compare German Schotter (“gravel”).

parole.significato: scrip, satchel, musette (a small leather bag with a shoulder strap)
parole.testo: Borrowed from German, specifically from Bavarian. Compare German Täschel.
Borrowing from German, specifically from Bavarian, compare trager (“peddler, merchant”).
